extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging researchers studying humor and affective processing
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, analyzing, and interpreting an event-related fMRI experiment that measures neural and behavioral responses to humorous (cartoon) stimuli and compares sex differences in activation. Covers stimulus selection, behavioral measures, scanning parameters, preprocessing, statistical thresholds, ROI/time-series and parametric analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection and screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty healthy subjects (mean age, 22 years ± 1.9; 10 females). All subjects were right-handed native English speakers screened for history of psychiatric or neurological problems by using Symptom Checklist-90-R. Written informed consent was obtained and procedures complied with Human Subjects Committee guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit demographically similar subjects, screen for psychiatric/neurological history (SCL-90-R used here), restrict to right-handed native speakers if language/verbal decoding is relevant; obtain IRB approval and informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection and pre-rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants of similar age and background selected 42 of the funniest cartoons from a portfolio of 130 cartoons, rating each cartoon for simplicity and visual clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preselect stimuli using independent raters matched to participant demographics; assess simplicity and visual clarity to avoid confounds from stimulus complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus types and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Stimuli were verbal and nonverbal achromatic cartoons; the majority were of the violation-of-expectation type, and most were captioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document stimulus modality (verbal/nonverbal), visual properties (achromatic), and joke type (violation-of-expectation) because these influence cognitive processes engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation timing and event-related design
rubrics_metrics.description: Each cartoon was presented in random order for 6,000 ms in an event-related paradigm. A jittered interstimulus interval (ISI) of 2,000, 4,000, and 6,000 ms was varied randomly and counterbalanced across events. Each full session lasted 15 min and 4 s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fixed stimulus duration appropriate for comprehension (6 s here), randomize order, jitter ISI to decorrelate events, and ensure session length fits scanner/time constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task instructions and in-scan response
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects were told to respond with the press of a button if they found the cartoon funny or not during the scan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a simple binary in-scan behavioral response (funny/unfunny) to link subjective judgment to BOLD responses; ensure response hardware and instructions are standardized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-scan intensity ratings (parametric measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the scan, subjects ranked each cartoon they had found funny during the scan on a 1-to-10 'funniness' scale. These subjective rankings were used to parametrically covary humor intensity with associated linear changes in BOLD signal intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect post-scan continuous ratings to enable parametric modulation analyses relating stimulus intensity to neural activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral measures reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral metrics included the number of stimuli rated funny, subjective degree of funniness (1–10), and response time (RT) to funny and unfunny stimuli.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report frequency measures, subjective intensity, and RTs; test between-group differences (t-tests) and within-group effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling stimulus presentation errors / completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: 12 funny and 2 unfunny cartoons were missing because of a script error; during the scan 30 funny and 40 unfunny were presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log presentation errors and missing stimuli; account for them in analysis and report their impact on counts and statistical power.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Images acquired on a 3-T scanner using 28 axial slices (4-mm thick, 0.5-mm skip) parallel to AC-PC with TR = 2,000 ms, TE = 30 ms, flip angle = 80°, 1 interleave, field of view 200×200 mm2, matrix 64×64, giving in-plane spatial resolution 3.125 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report scanner strength, slice geometry, TR/TE, flip angle, interleaving, FOV and matrix to allow replication and to understand temporal/spatial resolution trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion control / head stabilization
rubrics_metrics.description: A custom-built head holder was used to prevent head movement associated with laughter. To maximize magnetic-field inhomogeneity, an automatic shim was applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement head stabilization particularly when stimuli may evoke motion (laughter); perform shimming for field homogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image reconstruction and preprocessing
rubrics_metrics.description: Inverse Fourier transform reconstructed images for each time point. SPM99 was used to preprocess all fMRI data, including realignment, normalization to stereotaxic Talairach coordinates, and smoothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard preprocessing pipeline: image reconstruction, motion realignment, spatial normalization, and smoothing using established software (SPM99 here). Document versions and parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-level and second-level statistical modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical parametric maps were first generated for funny vs. unfunny stimuli for each subject by using a general linear model. Second, random effects analysis was performed to determine each subject's voxel-wise activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GLM at first level and random-effects (group-level) analysis for population inference; specify contrasts of interest (funny vs unfunny).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-brain cluster significance thresholds and multiple-comparison correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant clusters of activation were determined by using the joint expected probability distribution with height (P < 0.05) and extent (P < 0.05) thresholds corrected at the whole-brain level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control family-wise error across the whole brain using combined height and extent thresholds (joint expected probability) and report corrected P-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voxel-level thresholding within clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of voxels in each cluster of interest, with z > 1.96 (P < 0.05), was determined for each contrast. An α level for significance of P < 0.05 (two-tailed) was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report voxelwise thresholds (z or t) used within clusters and the alpha level for two-tailed tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-of-interest (ROI) analysis and a priori ROI specification
rubrics_metrics.description: ROI analysis was performed by using group-wise activation clusters at the whole-brain level. A priori ROIs were specified (e.g., a 10-voxel NAcc subcluster from a previous study and a 477-voxel DLPFC cluster) for time-series analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a priori ROIs (from literature or prior contrasts) to conduct ROI time-series and parametric analyses; report coordinates and voxel counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-series analysis of ROIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Averaged time-series analysis for funny vs. unfunny activity was performed in a 10-voxel subcluster of the NAcc and a 477-voxel DLPFC cluster to compare male and female activation dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform ROI time-series analyses to visualize and statistically compare temporal BOLD responses across conditions and groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametric covariate analysis linking subjective ratings to BOLD
rubrics_metrics.description: Posthoc covariate analysis compared humor intensity (subjects' degree of funniness rankings) and BOLD signal magnitude; humor intensity was correlated with degree of NAcc activity in females but not in males.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parametric modulation with subjective ratings to probe linear relationships between perceived intensity and neural response; test group differences in covariation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth modeling for time-series statistical inference
rubrics_metrics.description: For each region-by-stimulus combination a quadratic growth model was fitted using maximum likelihood estimation with free parameters including fixed initial status, linear slope, quadratic slope, residual variances, and sex effects on growth parameters. Models with and without sex effects were compared by log-likelihood difference tests; a likelihood ratio test served as an omnibus test for sex differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit formal growth/curve models to ROI time-series and compare nested models (with/without group effects) via likelihood-ratio tests to test for group differences in temporal dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting activation peaks and anatomical localization
rubrics_metrics.description: Report cluster size (voxels), Talairach coordinates, Brodmann's areas, peak z or T scores, and P values for activation peaks (e.g., left STG BA38 at -51,17,-19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide stereotaxic coordinates, BA labels, statistical peak values, and cluster extents to localize activations precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrasts for group comparisons and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform group contrasts (females > males and males > females) and interpret observed differences (e.g., females showed greater activation in NAcc and left PFC; no regions showed significantly higher male activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly test opposite-direction contrasts and report null findings as well as positive ones; interpret in the context of hypothesized cognitive/affective processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking neural regions to cognitive/affective functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign functional roles: left temporal-occipital junction and temporal pole implicated in semantic processing and juxtaposition (comprehension); left IFG and DLPFC implicated in language processing and executive functioning (coherence); NAcc and mesolimbic regions implicated in reward and amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map activation loci onto functionally characterized networks (comprehension vs reward) to interpret how stimulus processing stages relate to observed BOLD patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral-statistical testing for equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Test for between-sex differences in behavioral measures using t-tests; here no significant difference was found in number of stimuli rated funny, degree of funniness, or mean RT between sexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include classical hypothesis tests comparing behavioral measures across groups to determine whether neural differences occur independent of overt behavioral differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternative explanations and generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that greater female activation might be nonspecific higher activation rather than task-specific; recommend future analysis to investigate whether activity differences are absent during nonreward-related tasks and caution about generalizing to other humor types and age ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss alternative interpretations (global activation differences), task specificity, and limits to generalization; propose follow-ups to test specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical interpretation using reinforcement/reward prediction models
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret NAcc differences using 'reward prediction error' coding: dopaminergic neurons respond most to unexpected rewards and negatively to omitted expected rewards, explaining sex differences in NAcc activation and RT patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting mesolimbic activation, consider computational models (reward prediction error) to link neural dynamics to expectation and learning mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and funding disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Report ethical compliance, funding sources (NIH grants, Howard Hughes fellowship), author contributions, and conflicts of interest (none declared).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include transparent statements about ethics, funding, author roles, and conflicts to contextualize research.
